newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5/9.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5/9.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 8.5/9.0 percent on Monday on ample liquidity, dealers said.
They said ample supply was mainly due to an early central bank injection of some 1.111 trillion rupiah into the market, driving short-dated swaps to fall.
One local bank dealer said, however, longer-term rates were relatively stable amid ample condition.
The central bank also did not offer overnight papers (SBIs) to set a downside limit for the ample market.

The central bank offered one-week SBIs at 11.25 percent, two-week at 11.50 percent, one-month at 12.50 percent, three-month at 13.25 percent, six-month at 13.50 percent and 12-month at 13.75 percent on Monday.
Dealers said the ample condition might be extended to Tuesday because of cheap tom/next swaps. Overnight swaps were at 0.15/0.20 and tom/next swaps at 0.32/0.33 points.
One- and three-month money were quoted at 13.00/13.25 and 14.00/14.25 percent, respectively.
Bond traders said prices were stable, with the benchmark PLN V/A bond still yielding 16.14 percent on Monday morning.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 9.74 percent, compared with 9.5 percent on Thursday.
